title: AudienceBundlePayload
description:
The payload of an audience bundle: the same meta as a policy bundle (version, `issuedAt`,
`notAfter`), its own schema and content.

AudienceBundleContent.description:
Everything the audience bundle asserts. RFC 8785 canonical form (ADR-0005); adding, removing,
renaming or retyping a field is a schema change.

AudienceCredential.description: How the consumer obtains and places the credential.

extraHeaders.description: Further headers set with fixed values.

header.description: The header the credential is placed in, a lowercase token. Unset means `authorization`.

placement.description: Where it is placed. Required: a misspelling must never fall back to a default.

source.description: Where it comes from, for the `secret` backend.

AudienceDefinition.description:
The definition of one audience: the spec of a `SandboxAudience`, and the content of its signed
bundle.

caRef.description: A CA bundle for an upstream on a private PKI.

endpoints.description:
Where the audience is reached, `host:port`, exact names only (L017). Every one must be in
the ceiling of each policy that grants the audience (L014).

maxTtlSeconds.description: The longest token lifetime any grant may have (L028), and no more than the ceiling's (L014).

rules.description: The widest any grant may be (L028). None means every method and path.

AudienceRef.description:
Which `SandboxAudience` the bundle defines. The namespace decides whether it is a platform or a
team audience, and the consumer derives that from its own configuration, never from a field
here (ADR-0020, decision 2).

uid.description: The incarnation, for the version floor (ADR-0008).

Backend.description: How the consumer obtains the credential, the vocabulary mediatore implements.

oneOf.description: The consumer mints a token with its own signing key. Platform audiences only (L022).
An operator-held credential, read from the source.
The requester's own credential, delegated with the claim. Platform audiences only (L022).
Entra ID On-Behalf-Of with the consumer's app registration. Platform audiences only (L022).
No credential: the audience is reached through the proxy, under its endpoints and rules.

notAfter.description:
The bundle is worthless after this instant. Bounded by the earliest active grant expiry, so a
relaxation lapses without any revocation mechanism.

ConfigMapKeyRef.description:
A key of a ConfigMap in the audience's own namespace (no namespace field, as for
[`SecretRef`]).

key.description: The key holding the PEM bundle.

oneOf.description: A username and a password or token, sent as HTTP Basic.

CredentialSource.description: Where the credential comes from: exactly one of the two.

oneOf.description: A Secret in the audience's namespace.

EndpointRule.description:
One HTTP rule for an endpoint (ADR-0013): a method, or `*` for any, and a path glob in which `*`
matches one segment and `**` zero or more, matched against the path without the query. The
shape mediatore's egress proxy uses (its ADR-0025).

HeaderPair.description: One header set on the upstream request with a fixed value.

name.description: The header name, a lowercase token (L026).

value.description:
The value, as sent: printable ASCII, no line break (L026). Published in the bundle as
written, so never a credential.

OpenBaoSource.description:
A path in the platform's OpenBao, read with the consumer's own identity. Platform audiences
only (L023).

oneOf.description: At the gateway, outside the pool VM.
In the pool VM's egress proxy: the credential sits in the VM's memory (L029 for a team).

SecretRef.description:
A Secret in the audience's own namespace. There is no namespace field on purpose: a reference
is always resolved where the audience lives (ADR-0020, decision 4).

tokenKey.description: The key holding the token or password.

usernameKey.description: The key holding the username, for `format: basic`.
